approved: Defence Legislation Amendment (RCDVS Implementation and Related Measures No. 2) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would implement reforms from the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide to improve wellbeing and safety for ADF members, veterans and their families.

It would amend the Defence Act 1903 and the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Act 2004 to expand health, data and transition support functions, and establish a legislative basis for Defence health services.
The bill includes mandatory discharge for ADF members convicted of sexual or other serious offences resulting in a prison sentence, and prevents those with such convictions from joining the ADF.
Adds a dedicated part to the Defence Act 1903 for health and wellbeing support.
Expands the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Commission's functions to include prevention and early intervention services.
Allows better use of data for research on suicide and wellbeing.
Clarifies information sharing for transition support and claims processing.
Establishes a legislative framework for Defence health services with quality assurance activities.
Enables Defence to directly engage with families who provide contact details and to provide benefits to former partners after separation.
Australian Defence Force members, veterans, their families, the Department of Defence, the Department of Veterans' Affairs, and the Defence and Veterans' Service Commission.

Moved the second reading of a bill implementing 15 recommendations of the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide and supporting 20 more. Proposed stronger information sharing with privacy safeguards, modernised Defence health governance, improved family and transition support, mandatory separation after imprisonment for serious violence or sexual offences, and enhanced oversight.

Presented the Selection of Bills Committee's seventh report and moved its adoption; the report recommended immediate referral of four bills concerning defence, health insurance and tax reform to Senate committees with reporting dates from 13 August to 7 October 2026, while an amendment proposed referring a workplace relations bill by 10 August.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Defence Legislation Amendment (RCDVS Implementation and Related Measures No. 2) Bill and the Statute Update Bill stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after adjournment of their second-reading debates.

Argued that the bill implements recommendations of the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide and should receive constructive, cautious support. Supported better information sharing, Defence health governance, family assistance, protections for victims-survivors and stronger integrity standards, while calling for strict privacy safeguards, effective oversight and scrutiny of the reforms' practical results.

Argued that the Defence Legislation Amendment (RCDVS Implementation and Related Measures No. 2) Bill 2026 would improve information sharing between Defence and DVA, support families, strengthen health services and implement 35 royal commission recommendations; opposing views criticised veteran claim delays and government support, while the bill was read a second time and reported without amendment.
